$comment: GENERATED negative vectors: representations both codecs must refuse by protocol/vectors/export_vectors.py, using the Python Protocol_Codec as the producer. Do not edit; regenerate with `python -m protocol.vectors.export_vectors`.

vectors.name: wire/empty
vectors.note: No bytes at all. Phase 0 has nothing to read, so the version is unreadable rather than unsupported, and the decode error names field 1.

vectors.name: wire/truncated
vectors.note: A valid message with its last byte removed.

vectors.name: wire/trailing-bytes
vectors.note: A valid message followed by a second item. A message is one item, so decoding the first and ignoring the rest would leave bytes unaccounted for.

vectors.name: value/duplicate-map-keys
vectors.note: Two entries with the same key, in ascending order so no ordering rule objects. The profile admits neither, because re-encoding could only emit one of them.

vectors.name: value/indefinite-byte-string
vectors.note: One chunk, indefinite head. A permissive reader returns the same bytes; the profile refuses it because the encoder could not have produced it.

vectors.name: value/non-shortest-integer
vectors.note: Integer 1 written with a two-byte head.

vectors.name: value/cbor2-key-order
vectors.note: Shortest-encoding-first, which is RFC 7049 3.9 and what cbor2 canonical=True still emits. The profile's encoding of the same map is a21818002000.

vectors.name: value/decoded-key-order
vectors.note: Byte-string keys in decoded order rather than encoded order.

vectors.name: exec.request/env.sorted-by-decoded-key
vectors.note: The nested map's keys are in decoded-byte order rather than encoded-byte order, which is the ordering rule RFC 8949 4.2.1 replaced. Phases 0 and 1 pass, so Phase 2's profile check is what must refuse it.

vectors.name: proc.start/env.sorted-by-decoded-key
vectors.note: The nested map's keys are in decoded-byte order rather than encoded-byte order, which is the ordering rule RFC 8949 4.2.1 replaced. Phases 0 and 1 pass, so Phase 2's profile check is what must refuse it.
